profile.reading:
This building at Carrer dels Artesans 7 in Cerdanyola del Valles, inside the Parc Tecnologic del Valles technology park north of Barcelona, is a working colocation data centre operated by the Spanish provider Adam. The bare name recorded in the source map data, simply Adam, is the operator's own trading name rather than a placeholder or a person's name. Adam's published facility sheet for the site, which the company calls PTV, gives the same street address, C/ Artesans 7, 08290 Cerdanyola del Valles, and the same address appears in the operator's PeeringDB facility record, listed as Adam - PTV under the organisation ADAM.

Adam publishes a short specification for the building. It lists a surface area of 3,000 square metres and 4 MW of electrical power. That 4 MW figure is presented on the operator's page as the site's electrical power and is not described as a separately measured IT load, so this registry records it as published electrical capacity for the building and not as IT load. Adam states the site is built to Tier III design criteria and holds ISO 27001, ISO 9001 and ISO 22301 certification along with Spain's Esquema Nacional de Seguridad at Medium grade. Fire protection uses very early smoke detection, described as VESDA, with suppression by the dielectric agent NOVEC 1230. The building has a minimum of three meet-me rooms reached over redundant routes, and Adam lists Telefonica, Colt, BT, Xarxa Oberta, Cellnex, Vodafone, Verizon, GTD, Orange, Aire Networks, Adamo and Lyntia among the carriers available there. The operator has separately announced the commissioning of a new hall at this site, numbered Sala 6.

Adam describes itself as founded in 1989, at the start selling computers assembled from components, becoming one of the first four internet service providers in Spain in 1995 and opening its first Barcelona data centre, of 500 square metres, in 2001. It launched a container based modular product called DataBOX in 2008 and an OpenStack based cloud platform in 2014, and opened a Madrid site at TecnoAlcala in 2020. In 2024 CVC DIF acquired a 100 percent stake in the company. Adam currently lists three operating data centres, this PTV building, a Barcelona city site at Travessera de Gracia 342 of 600 square metres and 1.5 MW, and the Madrid TecnoAlcala site, with a fourth under construction at Parc de l'Alba in Cerdanyola del Valles, planned for 7,500 square metres of neutral technical rooms and 5 MW of electrical power already contracted for its first phase.

Adam does not publish generator or UPS ratings, a utility service size, a PUE figure, a hall count or a commissioning date for the PTV building, and this registry does not estimate any of them. The mapped footprint corresponds to an industrial building drawn in 2022 and named in a 2024 edit by a Catalan mapper working from cadastral imagery and map notes.
profile.research_note: Major correction 2026-09-05. The prior page treated this row as an unidentifiable placeholder named after a person. It is not. Adam is a real Spanish colocation operator and its own PTV facility page gives the exact street address carried in the OSM tags, C/ Artesans 7, 08290 Cerdanyola del Valles, confirmed independently by PeeringDB facility 14233 (Adam - PTV, org ADAM). OSM provenance: way 1077515970 created 2022-07-10 by SackMike as building=yes in changeset 123446124 (comment: adding elements at the Parc Tecnologic and surroundings), then in changeset 150953938 on 2024-05-06 mapper jqngarcia added the name, address and telecom=data_center from JOSM using Ortofoto iCGC, Catastro Spain and map notes. Power discipline: the 4 MW is published by the operator as electrical power for the site, not as a stated IT load, and is recorded that way. WebSearch quota was exhausted for this session, so all research was done via operator site, sitemap, PeeringDB API and the OSM API.
